watches.name: Brunswick 38 'Orchid'
watches.description: Hand-built in Britain in small batches. Please note: the Brunswick 38 'Orchid' is currently out of stock and orders placed now will be shipping again from late-January Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick is an exacting object to create. It takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 . Case : 38mm, stainless steel, polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Pink-tinted mother of pearl, with black printing and hand-applied numerals Strap : Dark grey, Alcantara® , handmade / 5-link, stainless steel bracelet with screw links and butterfly clasp Movement : LJP D100, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 100 metres (10 ATM) CASE The Brunswick’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case has no flat surfaces. The case’s graceful curves are machined from 316L stainless steel, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish showcases the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' is manually wound each day using our bespoke ‘onion’-shaped winding crown, signed with the Fears Cypher. The crown’s fine grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. CASEBACK The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' comes with the option of either: Open exhibition caseback - offering an unobstructed view of the finely decorated movement housed inside. Closed caseback - offering the perfect canvas for personalisation with a custom engraving (please discover engraving options here ). DIAL The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' joins the iconic Brunswick 40 'Aurora' to form a family of limited-production Fears pieces that feature dials constructed from Pinctada Maxima (mother of pearl from the rarest oyster pearl shells). Each section of these dials have been hand-tinted on the underside to achieve a delicate shade of pale pink (reminiscent of the Pink Cymbidium orchid) that highlights the natural iridescence of the material. Expertly made in Germany, these dials are painstakingly formed by hand using mother of pearl originating from some of the worlds highest quality, rarest and most sought-after pearl oysters. The dial is made using two pieces of mother of pearl with the main dial and a prominent, sunken, sub-seconds at the 6 o'clock position. The effect of opting for two levels cut to different heights creates a subtle yet impactful difference that creates an elegant distinction in how the light plays with the dial. The hand-applied numerals are milled from a block of brass before being diamond polished and then coated in black gold, giving them a bright, black/brown/silver appearance. These numerals are realised in our custom ‘Edwin’ typeface, specially designed for Fears by our horological typographer and inspired by the many different typefaces the company has used throughout its history. Please Note Due the nature of these dials each is entirely unique and will vary slightly from the images shown. The Managing Director has personally checked all the mother of pearl dials we use to ensure each maintains the same level of beauty and brilliant in their natural iridescence. HANDS The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' features iconic ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands expertly made in Germany, they are milled from solid brass with a bevel cut down the centre using a diamond tool. This results in a highly polished surface that catches the light, giving excellent legibility in low-light conditions. These hands are finished in a coating of black gold that perfectly matches the polished 3D numerals. MOVEMENT The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' is powered by a Swiss-made, manual winding La Joux-Perret D100 movement. This movement is the top-grade version, with an extended 50 hour power reserve and finished with Côtes de Genève and blued screws. STRAP The Brunswick 38 'Orchid' is fitted with a handmade strap in either Storm Grey or Blush Pink, crafted from Alcantara® with tonal stitching that gives this watch an contemporary feel whilst retaining its elegance. Alcantara®

The Fears Brunswick 40.5 Jump Hour takes a similar form to the Alliance 01 , housed in an elegantly curvaceous cushion shaped case with a few tweaks on the original. The design of our iconic Brunswick Jump Hour now evolves with not just new dial colours but also a revised dial design that features a new minute track and different finishing options. Expertly made, the surface of the dial features a fine concentric guilloche engraved deeply in the central minute section. The disc displaying these numerals is coated in a bright white lacquer before the hours are printed in glossy black ink in Fears bespoke ‘Edwin’ typeface that's been enhanced for display in a round window. watches.name: Brunswick Midas II
watches.description: The Golden Fears Please note: this model has now been discontinued The Brunswick Midas II continued the legacy of elegance and luxury of the original Brunswick Midas (2018-2021). This evolution exudes opulence with a rich 22ct yellow gold-plated case perfectly complemented by a frosted 18ct yellow gold champagne dial (the gold-on-gold theme inspired by a 1973 watch from the Fears Archive). This limited production piece comes with two straps that can give either a classic 1970s look or a more contemporary feel. Case : 38mm, stainless steel, brushed and polished, 20mm lug width Case Finish : 22ct Yellow Gold-Plated Dial : Champagne colour, with black printing and hand applied numerals Strap : Fears Blue, barenia calf leather and Chalk Blue, alcantara ® , both handmade Movement : ETA 7001, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 100 metres (10 ATM) Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick is an exacting object to create. It takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 , and a dial colour used in the 1940s and 50s. CASE The Brunswick’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case has no flat surfaces. The case’s graceful curves are machined from 316L stainless steel, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish showcases the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. The Brunswick Midas II's case has then been meticulously plated in heavy layers of 22ct yellow gold by one of the UK's leading specialists (who applied the same plating to the prototype London 2012 Olympic Torch used to promote those momentous games). The Brunswick Midas II is manually wound each day using our bespoke ‘onion’-shaped winding crown, signed with the Fears Cypher. The crown’s fine grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. CASEBACK The Brunswick Midas II comes with the option of either: Open exhibition caseback - offering an unobstructed view of the finely decorated movement housed inside. Closed caseback - offering the perfect canvas for personalisation with a custom engraving (please discover engraving options here ). Please note; as per tradition, whilst the case has been gold-plated the caseback will remain in un-plated stainless steel with a spun finish. DIAL The Brunswick Midas II features a hand-finished champagne dial which reproduces the rich colour of the famous sparkling wine. Finished with layers of 18ct yellow gold, the dial has a golden warmth that blends seamlessly with the golden case giving a strong 1970s influence. Expertly made in Germany, the surface of the dial features a glass bead-blasted finish, giving a frosted appearance with a gentle sparkle. T his effect is complemented by the concentric circle finishing on the sunken sub-seconds, at 6 o’clock. The hand-applied numerals are milled from a block of brass before being diamond polished and then coated in black gold, giving them a bright, black/brown/silver appearance. These numerals are realised in our custom ‘Edwin’ typeface, specially designed for Fears by our horological typographer and inspired by the many different typefaces the company has used throughout its history. HANDS The Brunswick Midas II features iconic ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands expertly made in Germany. Skeletonised and finished in blue using physical vapor deposition, the colour of the hands changes in the light from almost black to electric blue. MOVEMENT The Brunswick Midas II is powered by a Swiss made, manual-winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. Each movement features blued screws and Côtes de Genève striping. STRAPS The Brunswick Midas II comes with two straps, each giving the golden watch a different look and feel: Fears Blue strap handcrafted from premium Barenia leather with tonal stitching, that when paired with the gold lends a classic feel to the watch. watches.name: Brunswick 40 Topper Edition 'Winter Lake'
watches.description: A Tribute to a Northern California Commenting on the launch of the new Fears x Topper Edition Series II: Tribute to Northern California range, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill, (4 th ) Managing Director of the Fears Watch Company, says, “In January 2023 I visited the Topper Jewelers store in Burlingame California to meet with Fears owners from the bay area. While there, the Caplan family kindly took me to different spots nearby to show me what winter in Northern California was really like. The warmth, hospitality, and incredible landscapes inspired this limited-edition collaboration with Topper Jewelers. As friends of Fears, we were compelled to pay tribute to the remarkable state and create another special 'Topper Edition' that captures the essence of my unforgettable experience in the United States and a visit that left an indelible mark on me.” Case : 40mm, stainless steel, brushed and polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Blue colour, white printing and hand-applied indices in 'California' style configuration (featuring X1-Grade Super-LumiNova) Straps : Blue, nubuck buffalo leather, handmade Movement : LJP G101, time only, automatic, 68hr power reserve Water Resistance : 150 metres (15 ATM) Limited Edition : 25 pieces Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick silhouette takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 . CASE The Brunswick 40’s elegant yet sporty 40mm cushion-shaped case has no flat surfaces. The case’s glancing curves are machined from 316L stainless steel, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish along with the hand grained finish applied to the top of the case’s corners showcase the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. Complementing the case is our bespoke ‘onion’-shaped winding screw down crown, signed with the Fears Cypher. Screwed into the case, the crown’s fine grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. Built with uprated proportions, the Brunswick 40 has 150m water resistance, allowing it to be swum in when the crown is screwed all the way in. DIAL With a deep, frigid blue that reflects the coldness of Lake Tahoe in the winter. This wet-feel lacquered dial is joined with glossy white painted indices and hands that contrast in the way the snow touches the water’s edge. HANDS The distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are milled from solid brass with a bevel cut down the centre using a diamond tool. This results in a highly polished surface that catches the light, giving excellent legibility in low-light conditions. These hands are painted white to match the indices and then filled with X1-Grade Super-LumiNova. MOVEMENT The Brunswick 40 is powered by a customised Swiss-made, automatic La Joux-Perret G101 movement (that has had the date function removed). Winding itself when worn on the wrist this movement boasts a generous power reserve of 68 hours and a decorated winding rotor. STRAP This limited edition was offered on a beautiful Blue Buffalo Nubuck strap. The leather for which was sourced from the Himalayas, has been tanned in the same way traditional way it has been for centuries, using organic materials (and not modern techniques that utilise chemicals). It is not stretched during the tanning process, so is thicker more hard-wearing as a result. Retaining the same durability of buffalo leather but paired the similar napped and velvety texture of suede, this makes for a strap that has it all; beauty, ruggedness and an luxurious feel. Lined in genuine Alcantara® dyed a deep shade of blue, this lining is supremely soft against the skin yet resistant against wear. The strap is fitted with a stainless steel pin buckle that is subtly engraved with our ‘Fears’ logo. watches.name: Archival 1930 'Perpétuel Edition'
watches.description: The Perpétuel Edition. Please note; at the time of writing there may still be the final few pieces remaining, please make contact with Perpétuel Gallery if you are interested in securing one. The Fears Archival 1930 ‘Perpétuel Edition’ is a captivating fusion, bringing together raised, hand-applied numerals with exquisite finishing in an Eastern Arabic type set. It's an exciting venture, creating something entirely new by combining the British Racing Green of the United Kingdom with Eastern Arabic numerals and acts as a delightful homage to our cherished Middle Eastern partners, Perpétuel. The watch is available to purchase directly from the Perpétuel Gallery . Case : 40 x 22 mm, stainless steel, brushed and polished, 20mm lug width Dial : British Racing Green colour, with Eastern Arabic appliques Strap : Green , premium barenia calf leather, handmade Movement : ETA 2360, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 30 metres (3 ATM) Limited Edition : 25 pieces total The Archival 1930 'Perpétuel Edition' involves a considerable amount of work on new-old-stock movements and hand-finishing and t his model is a proportional recreation of an art deco watch Fears made in 1930 . True to the original, each watch features an original vintage movement. With its elegant form it is a perfect luxury rectangular watch for men or women. CASE The slim, rectangular case has the same elegant proportions as the original from 1930. The new watch has been increased in size a little while maintaining all the important ratios of the original to suit modern tastes. The case is expertly machined from 316L Stainless Steel, in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. It too takes its inspiration from this 1924 gentlemen's cushion shaped watch that inspired the modern Brunswick family of watches that launched in 2017 and features an inverse black version of the originals white dial. Due to the success of the the '1924 Edition' and the overwhelming demand we received, we decided it was only right that we offer an alternative option for those who missed out. The Brunswick 38 'Silver Noir' will be also be cased in the same 925 Sterling Silver, individually numbered, hallmarked and be supplied with a special owners card. watches.description: Fears' first Onyx dial Hand built in Britain in small batches for Collective Horology, this Redcliff is a unique collaboration with our close friends in California and can only be purchased directly via their website . Taking its name from the Bristol district where the company was first founded in 1846, the new Fears Redcliff Collection is designed to be an elegant and sophisticated everyday timepiece. Case : 39.5mm, 316L stainless steel, brushed and polished , 20mm lug width Dial : Black onyx, stone dial, white & silver printing Strap : Black , premium barenia calf leather, handmade Movement : LJP G101, time only, automatic, 68hr power reserve Collective Horology Exclusive : Only available from Collective Horology Price (on a premium Barenia leather strap) - $3600 CASE The Redcliff 39.5 Onyx is housed in a contemporary round case with integrated lugs alongside a screw-down case back, bezel and crown. Spanning 39.5mm in diameter yet with a case thickness of only 10.57mm, this slim case is as elegant as the dial it houses. This case has its own special reference and differs slightly from our standard Redcliff case; a raised bezel to accommodate the thicker dial and additional polished sections to give this watch a dressier feel that is commensurate with the elevated status of an onyx dial. DIAL The Redcliff 39.5 Onyx marks the first time a hard stone dial has appeared on a Fears watch in our rich history. Each dial is crafted from a disc of genuine Black Onyx that possesses a mirror-like shine that is as opulent as it is reflective. Expertly made in Germany, each disc of onyx is carefully adhered to a brass backplate before being crafted in to a functional dial. Onyx is a microcrystalline stone that is formed in the gas cavities of lava with a multi-layered structure that is likened to that of the agates. Onyx is very durable and the stones hardness means it has strong scratch and chip resistance. A contemporary set of baton indices are then printed atop the onyx surface in white and silver ink (that contains actual real silver). Please note Due the nature of these dials each is entirely unique and will vary slightly from the images shown. The Managing Director has personally checked all the onyx dials we use to ensure each share the same clarity and lustre. HANDS The Redcliff 39.5 Onyx's distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are tri-bevelled and diamond polished before being finished in a coating of rhodium - the tri-bevelled edges will catch the light brilliantly, allowing the time to be read easily. MOVEMENT The Redcliff 39.5 Onyx is powered by a customised Swiss-made, automatic La Joux-Perret G101 movement (that has had the date function removed). Winding itself when worn on the wrist this movement boasts a generous power reserve of 68 hours and a decorated winding rotor concealed by a closed case back. STRAP The Redcliff 39.5 Onyx is fitted with a handmade Black strap crafted from a premium Barenia leather with tonal stitching and fold-over edges that gives this watch an even more luxurious and contemporary feel. The premium leather used for this strap takes its name from the village of Barr in Alsace, from where it originates. Traditionally used for saddles, this smooth calfskin leather requires a complex tanning process, known by only a small number of craftsmen. Lined in genuine Alcantara® dyed a deep shade of blue, this lining is supremely soft against the skin yet resistant against wear. This strap is finished with Fears' new bespoke pin buckle (featuring the Fears Cypher). Customise You can customise your Redcliff 39.5 Onyx with any strap designed for a 20mm lug width, including any strap from our range , which you can easily fit yourself without tools. Taking its name from the Bristol street where the company was first founded in 1846, the new Fears Redcliff Collection is designed to be an elegant and sophisticated everyday timepiece. Closed caseback - offering the perfect canvas for personalisation with a custom engraving (please discover engraving options here ). DIAL The Redcliff 39.5 Date ‘Boutique Edition’ features a Mallard Green dial that now becomes the third-offering in Fears’ series of boutique editions. This special dark green has hints of grey and blue that recreates the rich colours that adorn the head of the mallard drake duck. Expertly made in Germany, the colour of the dial is achieved using a galvanic coating of 99.9% pure silver before being hand-painted with a translucent varnish which incorporates drops of pigment to produce the exact desired tone. The main section of the dial features a sunburst finish to the surface with a finely-milled CNC grooves on the lowered chapter ring. White and silver printing contrast brightly against this unique take on green and ensure that despite sharing an exclusive colour, each of Fears ‘Boutique Editions’ are uniquely different. At 3 o’clock a date window is cut into the dial revealing a colour-matched date disc featuring numerals in our own bespoke ‘Edwin’ typeset. The window itself features a shallow bevel running around all four sides to aide legibility whilst reading the date and gives the optical illusion of it appearing larger. The baton indexes are crafted from a block of brass before being diamond polished and coated in precious rhodium. The 12 o'clock index also features a subtle reference to another great Bristolian historical reference (the shape and form of the towers that hoist the famous Clifton Suspension Bridge). Each indices has been hand-filled with X1-Grade Super-LumiNova in Switzerland before being carefully hand-applied to the dial. HANDS The Redcliff 39.5 Date's distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are tri-bevelled and diamond polished before in this example being finished in a coating of rhodium (thus matching the indices). During the day the tri-bevelled edges will catch the light brilliantly, allowing the time to be read easily. Whilst in low-light conditions, the bright X1-Grade lume (a first for the core collection) glows with a strong blue colour colour and stays charged throughout the night - making for the perfect travelling companion. MOVEMENT The Redcliff 39.5 Date is powered by a customised Swiss-made, automatic La Joux-Perret G100 movement. Winding itself when worn on the wrist this movement features a quick-set date, a generous power reserve of 68 hours and a decorated winding rotor. BRACELET & STRAPS The Redcliff 39.5 Date comes with both a bespoke 3-link stainless steel bracelet or a pewter grey barenia leather

Closed caseback - offering the perfect canvas for personalisation with a custom engraving (please discover engraving options here ). DIAL The Redcliff 39.5 Date Pewter Grey features a warm, mid-grey dial that complements the tone of the 316L steel case perfectly. Expertly made in Germany, the main section of the dial features a hand-brushed vertical finish to the surface with a finely-milled CNC grooves on the lowered chapter ring. The rhodium coating is complemented by sharp black printing with soothing cyan for the minute numerals (and matching seconds hand). At 3 o’clock a date window is cut into the dial revealing a colour-matched date disc featuring numerals in our own bespoke ‘Edwin’ typeset. The window itself features a shallow bevel running around all four sides to aide legibility whilst reading the date and gives the optical illusion of it appearing larger. The baton indexes are crafted from a block of brass before being diamond polished and then coated in black gold, giving them a warm, grey/black appearance. The 12 o'clock index also features a subtle reference to another great Bristolian historical reference (the shape and form of the towers that hoist the famous Clifton Suspension Bridge). Each indices has been hand-filled with X1-Grade Super-LumiNova in Switzerland before being carefully hand-applied to the dial. HANDS The Redcliff 39.5 Date Pewter Grey's distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are tri-bevelled and diamond polished before in this example being finished in a coating of black gold (thus matching the indices). During the day the tri-bevelled edges will catch the light brilliantly, allowing the time to be read easily. Whilst in low-light conditions, the bright X1-Grade lume (a first for the core collection) glows with a strong blue colour colour and stays charged throughout the night - making for the perfect travelling companion. MOVEMENT The Redcliff 39.5 Date is powered by a customised Swiss-made, automatic La Joux-Perret G100 movement. Winding itself when worn on the wrist this movement features a quick-set date, a generous power reserve of 68 hours and a decorated winding rotor. BRACELET & STRAPS The Redcliff 39.5 Date comes with both a bespoke 3-link stainless steel bracelet or a Azurro blue barenia leather strap, and with either choice will also be accompanied by and a 3D-woven textile strap. Bracelet Featuring solid screw links, the bracelet combines brushed and polished elements and has a substantial feel while the silky-smooth movement of the links ensure a comfortable fit around the wrist. The bracelet can be adjusted for a perfect fit with both 6mm and 8mm screw links but also adjusted 'on the move'

watches.name: Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition'
watches.description: The Sterling Fears watch. The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' takes its inspiration from this 1924 gentlemen's cushion shaped watch that inspired the modern Brunswick family of watches that launched in 2017. With this being the 100th anniversary it felt right to commemorate it with the first sterling silver cased Fears watch made since the 1920s. Just 10 pieces of these precious watches were made, each numbered, hallmarked and featuring a dial inspired and influenced by that of the original watch from 1924. Each watch also comes in a special commemorative packaging. Case : 38mm, Sterling Silver (925), polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Sterling white, lacquered finish with black printing Strap : Fears Blue, premium Barenia leather, handmade Movement : LJP D100, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 100 metres (10 ATM) Limited Edition : 10 pieces only Price : £3,950 (inc. VAT) Created exclusively for the Alliance of British Watch & Clockmakers British Watchmakers' Day and only available to purchase from the event. CASE The Brunswick '1924 Edition' is housed in our elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case and is made from solid Sterling Silver. Crafted entirely from this understated metal, the case’s glancing curves are machined from 925 sterling silver with a deep polish all over, highlighting the beauty of the metal. The case and the solid caseback each bear hallmarks from the London Assay Office, and, following a Fears tradition, these comprise the initials of the Managing Director when the watch was built (in this case: ‘NBS’ for our (4th) Managing Director, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill). The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’-shaped winding crown, also made from solid Sterling Silver, and into which is set a flawless diamond (which on Fears watches signifies a case made entirely from a precious metal). DIAL The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' features a hand-polished white lacquer dial, expertly made in Germany by one of the world’s finest dial makers. After the layers of white lacquer are applied, multiple layers of crisp black ink bring the dial to life using a numeral set inspired by the 1924 original. Down at 6 o’clock is the subsidiary seconds dial, and below it we'd ordinarily print ‘England’ to recognise the fact that every Fears watch is hand built in England (which this watch is of course). However, instead is the same logo from the 1920s printed at the top of dial making this the first watch from Fears' modern-era to have Bristol on the dial. HANDS The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' features iconic ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands expertly made in Germany. Skeletonised and finished in blue using physical vapor deposition, the colour of the hands changes from almost black to electric blue in the light. MOVEMENT The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' is powered by a Swiss-made, manual winding La Joux-Perret D100 movement. This movement is the top-grade version, with an extended 50 hour power reserve and finished with Côtes de Genève and blued screws. STRAP The Brunswick 38 '1924 Edition' is fitted with a handmade Fears Blue strap crafted from Barenia leather with tonal stitching and fold-over edges, lending a premium feel to the watch. The premium leather used for this strap takes its name from the village of Barr in Alsace, from where it originates. Traditionally used for saddles, this smooth calfskin leather requires a complex tanning process, known by only a small number of craftsmen. The strap is fastened by a bespoke and matching hallmarked sterling silver pin buckle. Lined in genuine Alcantara® dyed a deep shade of blue, this lining is supremely soft against the skin yet resistant against wear. The Brunswick is designed to fit all of the straps in our range , which you can easily fit yourself without tools. INDIVIDUALLY NUMBERED Each watch we make carries a unique serial number. watches.name: Redcliff 'Edwin Edition'
watches.description: Edwin Fear, our eponymous founder, was born on 21 st December 1823, so this year marks the 200th anniversary of the year of his birth and we were keen to commemorate this important milestone with a special watch. As it was the original Redcliff model that Edwin’s great-great-great-grandson, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill, chose to re-established Fears Watch Company with in 2016, this felt like the most appropriate tribute to commemorate the legacy of Edwin. Whilst the Redcliff 'Edwin Edition' retains many of the hallmarks of the original Redcliff series it is distinctly different at the same time. The crisp white numerals give a classic look that with its glossy black lacquer dial combine to create a dress-style watch with an equally contemporary feel - an elegantly understated timepiece that Edwin certainly would have been proud of. Case : 38mm, stainless steel, polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Black, polished lacquer, with white printing Strap : Black, goat leather, handmade Movement : Ronda 512, time only, quartz Water Resistance : 50 metres (5 ATM) Limited Edition : 200 pieces total CASE The Redcliff 'Edwin Edition' featured an elegant and slim 38mm round case. Machined from 316L stainless steel in Switzerland, the case had a high polish finish to all surfaces, except the case back which has a beautiful spun finish and deep commemorative engraving with the watch’s unique serial number. Measuring just 8.5mm thick, this Redcliff was designed to slip under cuffs easily with its flat sapphire crystal. DIAL The Fears 'Edwin Edition' features a glossy black dial achieved through a highly-polished lacquer finish. Printed on the dial are bold yet elegantly understated R oman numerals (a first for Fears in the modern-era) that are inspired by a 1920's Fears station clock from our archive in Bristol. HANDS Using classic sword shaped hands, painted in gloss white, that perfectly complement the elegance of the dial, case and numerals. MOVEMENT The Redcliff 'Edwin Edition' is powered by an all metal, Swiss-Made, quartz Ronda 512 movement, that simply displays the hours and minutes. Supremely accurate and reliable, the Ronda 512 is powered by a mercury-free Swiss-made battery. STRAP The Redcliff 'Edwin Edition' is offered on a classic black goat leather strap, that perfectly complements the glossy black of the dial. Handcrafted from supple goat leather from the Madras region of India. Goat leather is ideal for watch straps due to its pliant yet strong nature, which allows the strap to be made exceptionally thin. The Redcliff ‘Edwin Edition’ was designed to fit all of the straps in our range , which you can easily fit yourself without tools. ENGRAVED CASEBACK Each watch we make carries a unique serial number, which on this model forms part of the caseback engraving designed specifically for this limited-edition watch Please note; this release is a limited-edition (200 pieces total) but not individually numbered, so whilst your watch will have an unique serial number (as all Fears watches do) they are not individually numbered out of 200. FEARS x CASED IN TIME CASE Any Fears watch is a precious item, so the Redcliff 'Edwin Edition' will be supplied in our Fears branded Cased in Time case. Cased In Time cases are the perfect safe storage for your watches, ideal for nights away, holidays and transportation. They offer 360-degree protection due to the rugged outer shell and softly sculpted interior.

watches.name: Archival 1930
watches.description: SOLD OUT The Archival 1930 has sold out, however, you might find one at one of our Fears Authorised Stockists , please contact us here . The rectangular Fears watch. The Archival 1930 involves a considerable amount of work on new-old-stock movements and hand-finishing and as such they are made in small batches. Created to coincide with the 175th Anniversary of the founding of Fears, the Archival 1930 is a proportional recreation of an art deco watch Fears made in 1930 . True to the original, each watch features an original vintage movement. With its elegant form it is a perfect luxury rectangular watch for men or women. Case : 40 x 22 mm, stainless steel, brushed and polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Vintage champagne colour, with black printing Strap : Oxblood red, Bristol calf leather, handmade Movement : ETA 2360, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 30 metres (3 ATM) Limited Edition : 136 pieces total CASE The slim, rectangular case has the same elegant proportions as the original from 1930. The new watch has been increased in size a little while maintaining all the important ratios of the original to suit modern tastes. The case is expertly machined from 316L Stainless Steel, in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. This precisely milled case is then finished in a combination of linearly brushed and highly polished surfaces. This long, slim watch sits comfortably on the wrist thanks to its curved profile. Just like the 1930 original, both the crystal and case back have a matching curvature that follows the contours of the wrist perfectly. The tip of the winding crown, used to wind the watch each day, is deeply engraved with the Fears ‘pipette’ logo. DIAL A close reproduction of the 1930 original, the dial has a distinctive Art Deco design, reflecting the glittering age in which it was first created. To capture the original’s look and details first the dial’s base is polished and plated in 18ct Yellow Gold, and then the rest of the dial is layered on top. This results in the real gold border shining through the smooth, matte Champagne finish that is treated to a light 18ct yellow gold plating. The ‘Deco’ numerals that share the slim proportions of the case are printed in crisp glossy black, giving excellent contrast. We call this concoction of gold, ‘Vintage Champagne’. HANDS Expertly milled before being diamond polished, the solid ‘Fears-shaped’ hands feature a central bevel down their length. This bevel helps them catch the light beautifully. The rich bluing offers great contrast with the light dial that increases legibility and aids telling the time. MOVEMENT The Archival 1930 is powered by an original ‘new old stock’ movement that Fears used in the past. The ETA 2360 movements date back to the 1960s and having never been used previously have undergone a full rebuild and reconditioning in the workshop while receiving an upgraded mainspring to improve reliability. Please note We expect timekeeping to be within +/-20 seconds a day, in-keeping with the original specification of the movement. STRAP Each Archival 1930 is paired with a handmade Bristol Leather strap in a traditional Oxblood Red, crafted in an art deco style like the original would have been, with no padding and with ‘box-style’ stitching. This premium strap uses calf leather that has been vegetable tanned in Britain’s oldest vegetable tannery, Bristol’s Thomas Ware & Sons to our own shade of this vintage red tone. The strap is lined in Fears Blue Alcantara®, offering a soft and comfortable feel against the skin. The Strap is fastened with a vintage shaped stainless steel pin buckle, which has received a linear brushing to its sides, matching the finish on the sides of the watch’s case. The final flourish comes in the form of a 1930s Fears logo deeply engraved on the polished top of the buckle. Strap Size Standard: Fits wrists approx. 172 - 206mm (6.7" - 8.1") Shorter: Fits wrists approx. 163 - 195mm (6.3" - 7.5") INDIVIDUALLY NUMBERE

Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick 40 takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 . This sportier iteration of the Brunswick is the perfect all-round watch, taking you from beach to boardroom with ease. The case’s glancing curves are machined from 316L stainless steel, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish along with the hand grained finish applied to the top of the case’s corners showcase the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. Complementing the case is our bespoke ‘onion’-shaped winding screw down crown, signed with the Fears Cypher. Screwed into the case, the crown’s fine grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. Built with uprated proportions, the Brunswick 40 is 150m water resistant, allowing it to be swum in when the crown is screwed all the way in. CASEBACK The Brunswick 40 'Aurora' comes with the option of either: Open exhibition caseback - offering an unobstructed view of the finely decorated movement (and custom Fears Blue rotor adorned with the Bristol flower). Closed caseback - offering the perfect canvas for personalisation with a custom engraving (please discover engraving options here ). DIAL The Brunswick 40 'Aurora' is the first mother of pearl dial to appear on a Fears watch in our 177-year history. Each dial is crafted from two pieces of Pinctada Maxima (mother of pearl from the rarest oyster pearl shells) with each section hand-tinted on its underside to achieve a special and unique shade of blue that highlights the natural iridescence of the material. Expertly made in Germany, the surface of the dial is on two levels cut to different heights (a subtle difference that creates a huge distinction in how the light plays with the dial). These dials are painstakingly formed by hand using mother of pearl originating from some of the worlds highest quality, rarest and most sought-after pearl oysters. The hand-applied numerals are milled from a block of brass before being diamond polished and then coated in rhodium. These numerals are realised in our custom ‘Edwin’ typeface, specially designed for Fears by our horological typographer and inspired by the many different typefaces the company has used throughout its history. Please note Due the nature of these dials each is entirely unique and will vary slightly from the images shown. The Managing Director has personally checked all the mother of pearl dials we use to ensure each maintains the same level of beauty and brilliant in their natural iridescence. HANDS The Brunswick 40 'Aurora's distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are milled from solid brass with a bevel cut down the centre using a diamond tool. This results in a highly polished surface that catches the light, giving excellent legibility in low-light conditions. These hands are finished with a coating of rhodium that perfectly matches the polished 3D numerals. MOVEMENT The Brunswick 40 is powered by a customised Swiss-made, automatic La Joux-Perret G101 movement (that has had the date function removed). Winding itself when worn on the wrist this movement boasts a generous power reserve of 68 hours and a decorated winding rotor. watches.name: Chocolate Brown
watches.description: Our straps are meticulously handcrafted by a family-run atelier in Belgium specialising in beautiful, premium watch straps. Leather Handcrafted from premium Buffalo leather (sourced from the Himalayas) and tanned in the same way it has been for centuries, using organic materials (and not modern techniques that utilise chemicals). It is not stretched during the tanning process, so is thicker and more durable and hard-wearing as a result. Colour Presented in Chocolate Brown, a warm, rich brown reminiscent of milk chocolate. Surface Finish Buffalo leather has a more distinct and deeper grain than calf leather and is characterised by its rich tone and striking appearance. When cared for this leather will last a lifetime and develop a rich patina, only enhancing it as time goes on. Lining Lined in our signature Fears Blue Alcantara and embossed with both our logo and ‘Handmade in Belgium’. Buckle Please note; the image shows our legacy buckle whereas this strap is now finished with Fears' new bespoke pin buckle (featuring the Fears Cypher). Size Designed to fit all Fears Redcliff, Brunswick and Archival watches, this strap will also fit any watch with a 20mm lug width . The strap is available in two sizes: Standard fits wrists measuring 178 - 210mm (approx.) Shorter fits wrists measuring 164 - 197mm (approx.) Fit yourself Featuring Quick-Release spring bars , our straps can be fitted and removed from the watch using no tools. This means you can change it over in a matter of moments with no hassle.

watches.name: Brunswick 40 White Topper Edition
watches.description: The coolest Fears watch. Limited to 25 pieces, this special collaboration commemorated a long-awaited debut in North America. As the eleventh “Topper Edition” co-designed and offered exclusively to Topper Jewelers , this Brunswick followed the blueprint of the brand’s Brunswick, re-sized to a newly engineered 40mm case featuring a series of sporty new twists in the form of a hybrid "California" dial with generous luminosity, 100 meters of water resistance, and a Swiss-made automatic movement, tailored for a lifetime of adventure. CASE The Brunswick 40’s elegant yet sporty 40 mm cushion-shaped case has no flat surfaces. The case’s glancing curves are machined from 316L stainless steel in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. With a hand grained finish applied to the top of the case showcasing the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. Complementing the case is our bespoke ‘onion’-shaped winding crown, the crown’s fine grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. DIAL The Brunswick 40 White Topper Edition features a high-polish liquid white lacquer with applied diamond-cut hour markers in a "California" style configuration. Featuring Roman numerals at the top half, and traditional Arabic numerals along the bottom. The Markers are filled with Swiss X1 Superluminova (blue emission). The numerals are applied to the dial by hand, after being diamond polished to a mirror shine and coated in Rhodium. HANDS The Brunswick 40 White Topper Edition bears distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are coated in rhodium, hand-filled with Swiss X1 Superluminova. MOVEMENT The Brunswick 40 is powered by a Swiss made, automatic winding ETA 2824-2 movement. watches.name: Brunswick 'Ice'
watches.description: The coolest Fears watch. The Brunswick Ice is a true one-of-a-kind watch, created for a wonderful cause. A piece unique straight from the mind of (4th) Managing Director, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill. Donated for the inaugural EveryWatch auction ( 23 August 2023) to raise money for Maggie’s Centres . CASE The Brunswick’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case has no flat surfaces, with even the solid case back having a gentle sweep. The case’s graceful curves are machined from 316L stainless steel, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish showcases the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. The Brunswick is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’-shaped winding crown. The crown’s grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. DIAL The Brunswick Ice features an extraordinary bespoke Ice Blue dial tone, created using a special kind of lacquer with different drops of pigment added to achieve the exact desired tone. Expertly made in Germany, the surface of the dial features a light-catching sunburst finish radiating from the centre. This finish works with the subtle cool tones of Ice Blue lacquer to make different segments of the dial shine lighter and darker. This effect is complemented by the concentric circle finishing on the sunken sub-seconds at 6 o’clock. The numerals are applied to the dial by hand, after being diamond polished to a mirror shine and coated in Rhodium. Each numeral, with its bright silver colour, has the appearance of a small ingot of precious metal resting on the dial’s colourful surface. The numerals are realised in our custom ‘Edwin’ typeface, specially designed for Fears by our horological typographer and inspired by the many different typefaces the company has used throughout its history. HANDS The Brunswick Ice’s distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are coated in rhodium with a solid bevelled finish identical to the hands on the solid platinum Brunswick. MOVEMENT The Brunswick is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, with Côtes de Genève striping and Rhodium plating. Bracelet The Brunswick Ice is fitted to a bespoke stainless steel 5-link bracelet with expertly brushed and polished links. This particular bracelet is equally unique as the links alternative between polished and brushed in a different pattern to the regular bracelet. Featuring solid screw links, the bracelet has a substantial feel while the silky-smooth movement of the links ensure a comfortable fit around the wrist. The bracelet can be micro-adjusted with both the 8 mm and 6 mm links provided, ensuring a perfect fit. The bracelet is secured to the wrist using a trigger-release butterfly style clasp with the Bristol flower enamelled discreetly inside the blades. EVERYWATCH ENGRAVED The Brunswick Ice is finished with a subtle closed back - engraved with the EveryWatch emblem.

watches.name: Brunswick Pure
watches.description: The pure Fears watch. CASE The Brunswick Pure takes the classic Brunswick’s elegant 38 mm cushion-shaped case and coats it in black DLC (Diamond-Like Carbon). This striking black coating makes the case scratch resistant while allowing the beautiful finishing of the Brunswick’s stainless steel case to shine through. DIAL The Brunswick Pure features a hand-polished white lacquer dial, expertly made in Germany by one of the world’s finest dial makers. Unlike our Brunswick White, the Brunswick Pure’s dial is devoid of any ornamentation resulting in a pure, clean surface with only the sunken subsidiary seconds dial at 6 o’clock to break up the vibrancy of the lacquered surface. HANDS The Brunswick’s distinctive ‘Fears’-shaped hands are skeletonised before being painted in a special matt black paint. The matt black contrasts beautifully with the glossy brightness of the white lacquer dial. MOVEMENT The Brunswick is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, with Côtes de Genève striping and Rhodium plating. STRAP The Brunswick Pure is the first Fears watch ever to be fitted with an animal-free strap. This soft and supple strap is hand made from a leather-like material that is created using apples (yes, as in the fruit!). Lined in cork, this is the first example of a new animal-free strap range launching in 2023. The Brunswick is designed to fit all of the straps in our range, which you can easily fit yourself without tools. INDIVIDUALLY NUMBERED Each watch we make carries a unique serial number. Engraved between the 20mm lugs at 12 o’clock, this number helps us identify your watch and its history. BRITISH BOX For decades Fears presented watches in a dark blue box with a cream-coloured lining. We are delighted to continue this tradition today. The Brunswick Pure is presented in a bespoke wooden box, crafted in Britain from English Ash, which is stained Fears Blue. Lined in genuine cream suede, the watch sits proudly on a special cushion.

watches.name: Brunswick Brown
watches.description: Year produced: 2021 Numbers produced: 5 Hand built in Britain in a limited run of only five watches, to celebrate the 175th Anniversary of the original founding of the company in 1846. Graceful and complex, like the other members of the Brunswick family, this is an exacting object to create. It takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924. CASE The Brunswick’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case has only one flat surface - the rear sapphire glass. Its glancing curves are machined from 316L stainless steel in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish belies the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. The Brunswick is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’-shaped winding crown. Made in Switzerland, the crown’s grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. On the solid caseback of the Brunswick Brown is our 175th Anniversary logo, laser engraved to give it a three-dimensional look with a brown hue complimenting the dial on the other side. Also engraved is the edition number, identifying each watch as part of this limited run. DIAL The Brunswick Brown features a Burnt Ochre dial that undergoes an extraordinary 59 production processes to achieve its multi-tone colour, which we call Burnt Ochre. Part of this involves the dial receiving a galvanic coating of Rhodium, followed by a clear lacquer featuring pigment with a bespoke shade of brown. Along with the hand-brushed ring where the numerals sit, these combine to give the effect of an almost wood-like finish. The numerals and alternate dots, which are applied to the dial by hand, are machined from brass and mirror polished before being hand painted in cream enamel, reminiscent of a 1930s British range cooker. The result is a smooth yet bold juxtaposition with the dial tone. HANDS The Brunswick Brown’s distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are finished by a watchmaker, giving them a depth and detail not found in mass-produced, stamped watch hands. Each set of hands is subtly skeletonised before being polished to a mirror shine and painted in the same cream enamel to match the numerals. Fears is one of only a handful of British watch brands that construct watch hands in-house, in the UK. MOVEMENT The Brunswick is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, with Côtes de Genève striping and Rhodium plating. Once the movement has been re-assembled and thoroughly tested, it receives Fears’ ‘Golden Pipette’, which is handmade and applied to the bridge. STRAP The Brunswick Brown comes with three straps, each of which gives the watch a different and distinctive look. Bund strap : having its origins in military aviation, this style of strap features an extra band of leather between the watch case and the skin. This strap is handmade in Belgium from European Buffalo nubuck, giving a soft texture, and is a rich, chocolate brown, with a contrasting ivory stitch; these two colours match the dial, numerals, and hands, bringing them out. The strap is lined in Fears Blue Alcantara and has a Fears pipette laser engraved on the buckle. watches.name: Brunswick Midas Silver
watches.description: The golden Fears Our flagship watch - the Brunswick Midas Silver. We hand make only ten Midas watches in total each year across the two dial variants. The complexity of the curvaceous case and level of hand finishing required for each watch not only takes time but also high levels of skill. Housed in an elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case inspired by a watch Fears made in 1924 - one of the most graceful shapes a watch can take. Case Starting life from a block of marine-grade Phosphor Bronze, each case is first machined before undergoing an entire day of hand-polishing by an expert watchmaker. The watchmaker’s skill results in the beautiful curves of Midas and gives it its brilliant shine. The finished Bronze case then receives its “Dual-Gold” coating; first a layer of 18ct rose gold then a layer of 9ct yellow gold. These two layers of differing golds give the watch is unique warm yellow gold colour – truly special. The Midas is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’ shaped winding crown. Made in Switzerland, the crown’s grooves and "Dual-Gold" coating catch the light, adding a little sparkle to the edge of the case. The watch features a solid stainless steel caseback, with a spun, circular grained finish, which echoes those found on the rolled gold Fears watches produced in the 1960s and 70s. Dial The Brunswick Midas Silver features a brilliant silver tone on the dial, thanks to a Rhodium coating, along with delicate, vertical brushing, applied by hand, making each watch unique. At six o’clock is the sunken sub-seconds, finished in concentric circles. The numerals receive their own “Dual-Gold” coating, before being applied by hand, and these, together with the finishing of the dial, create, in the right light, the illusion of a pale champagne colour. The elegant, classic set of numerals was designed specially for Fears by a horological typographer, inspired by the many different typefaces Fears has used throughout its history. Hands “Dual-Gold” also finds its way onto ‘ Fears ’ shape hands, which are hand finished (pun intended) by a watchmaker giving them a depth and detail not found in mass produced, stamped watch hands. Fears is rare in making its watch hands in-house in the UK, something done by only a handful of British watch brands. Movement The Midas is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. The design of this accurate movement was first penned in the 1970s and its reliability results in it being a popular choice today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, applying a ‘stippled’ surface finish along with “Dual-Gold” plating. Once the movement has been re-assembled and thoroughly tested it then receives the ‘Golden Pipette’. Strap Each Midas Silver is paired with a handmade Bristol Leather strap in Chocolate Brown. This premium strap uses calf leather, vegetable tanned in Britain’s oldest tannery in Bristol. The strap is fastened with a “Dual-Gold” buckle that perfectly matches the warmth of the case. Individually Numbered Each watch Fears makes carries a unique serial number. Engraved between the 20mm lugs at 12 o’clock, this number helps us identify your watch and its history through our master database. The serial numbers are sequential, meaning no two watches, regardless of batch, will ever carry the same number. BRITISH BOX For decades Fears presented their watches in a dark blue box with a cream-coloured lining. We are delighted to continue this tradition today. The Brunswick Midas Silver is presented in a bespoke wooden box, crafted in Britain from English Ash, which is stained Fears Blue. Lined in genuine cream suede, the watch sits proudly on a special cushion. With minimal branding, the outside of the lid reveals a hidden map of Brunswick Square when held in a certain light. A truly special wrist watch. REVIEWS You can read a hands on review of the Brunswick Midas Silver by Worn & Wound here .

watches.name: Brunswick White Series 1 (2017)
watches.description: The first Brunswick Years produced: 2017-2018 Numbers produced: 67 The first mechanical watch of the new Fears era. Produced in very small batches, the Brunswick Series 1 shares a lot of aesthetic characteristics with our current Brunswick White , its successor. CASE The Brunswick Series 1’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case had only one flat surface - the rear sapphire glass. Each case was first machined in the UK before undergoing several days of polishing and finishing by one watchmaker. A truly hand finished watch, requiring a high level of skill to make each watch. DIAL The Brunswick Series 1 featured a cold resin enamel dial with a milky white glossy dial surface. Each dial was made entirely in the UK with a high rate of rejection in its creation. Once the enamel was set and polished the dial was printed, using a bolder version of the classic numeral set used on the Brunswick White and first used by Fears in 1946 . HANDS The Brunswick Series 1 used the same distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands as the Brunswick White . Made and finished in our workshops by a watchmaker, giving them a depth and detail not found in mass-produced, stamped watch hands. Each set of hands is subtly skeletonised before being thermally blued by a flame. This traditional method of thermally hardening the steel results in a blue unique to each Brunswick, from almost black to electric blue in the light. Fears is one of only a handful of British watch brands that construct watch hands in-house, in the UK. MOVEMENT The Brunswick is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, with Côtes de Genève striping and Rhodium plating. The movement in the first 14 watches was surrounded by a golden movement ring. This limited run was a reference to the number at Number 14 Brunswick Square, from where the watch takes its name from. The remaining watches featured a movement ring plated in bright Rhodium. From watch No. 20 onwards the movement received a Fears ‘Golden Pipette’. STRAP The first batches of Brunswick Series 1s were supplied on a Fears Custom strap made to the owner’s wishes. The following batches were offered on handmade Alligator straps in a range of precious stone colours before the Bristol Leather straps were introduced in late 2018. The Brunswick Series 1 is designed to fit all of the straps in our range , which you can easily fit yourself without tools. Replacement Straps Straps that are compatible with the Brunswick (Series 1) can be purchased from here . INDIVIDUALLY NUMBERED Each watch we make carries a unique serial number. The first 19 watches carried their serial number on an engraved movement ring, visible through the exhibition case back. Subsequent watches carried their serial number between the 20mm lugs at 12 o’clock. ENGRAVED PERSONAL TO YOU Fears offers an engraving service whereby a watch can be made personal to its new owner. We work with one of the UK's leading 3D laser engravers who can engrave initials, a date, or a special verse on your watch. Please contact us here to discuss how we can make your watch extra special.

watches.name: Redcliff "Streamline" (2019)
watches.description: The vintage Fears watch Year produced: 2019 Pieces produced: 100 A limited-edition watch created to commemorate the first 1,000 days since Fears relaunched. CASE The Redcliff “Streamline” featured a slim, elegant, 38mm round case. Machined from 316L stainless steel in Switzerland, the case had a high polish finish to the bezel and lugs. The case sides featured a contrasting horizontal graining, undertaken in our UK workshops. Measuring just 8.5mm thin, the Redcliff “Streamline” was designed to slip under cuffs easily with its flat sapphire crystal. DIAL The Redcliff “Streamline” featured our most vintage-inspired dial to date. Taking inspiration from a watch produced by Fears in 1946 called the “Streamline”, the dial features a bespoke set of numerals picked out in gilt printing. Sparkling in the sunlight, the gilt numerals use the same typeset as the original. The dial’s base featured a distinctive vertical graining with a special Forties Silver colour made using 18ct Gold plating. The warm, antique colour gave the Redcliff “Streamline” its own distinctive character. HANDS The Redcliff “Streamline” used the distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands, painted in a deep, gloss black. The hour and minute hands were filled with Super-LumiNova luminous materials to help with reading the time in the dark. The central seconds hand was painted in red. This was in homage to the original, which had a red central seconds hand to aid with timing events. The seconds hand included a micro ‘Pipette’ as its counterbalance. MOVEMENT The Redcliff “Streamline” was powered by an all metal, Swiss made, quartz Ronda 515 movement. Supremely accurate and reliable, the Ronda 515 is powered by a mercury-free Swiss made battery. Battery Change If your watch requires a new battery then you can purchases a battery change form the Fears Service Division here . STRAP Each Redcliff “Streamline” was paired with a vintage-style Mink Brown strap from our Goat’s leather collection. watches.name: Brunswick Blue
watches.description: The brilliant Fears watch. Hand built in Britain in small batches. Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick Blue is an exacting object to create. It takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 . CASE The Brunswick’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case has only one flat surface - the rear sapphire glass. Its glancing curves are machined from 316L stainless steel in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. The depth of the polish belies the sophistication of the machinery and the skill of the operator. The Brunswick is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’-shaped winding crown. Made in Switzerland, the crown’s grooves catch the light, adding a touch of radiance to the edge of the case. DIAL The Brunswick Blue features an extraordinary Fears Blue dial that undergoes 56 production processes. At first glance, the Germany made dial appears to have a two-tone sector layout, but when tilted it becomes a tri-tone – all from one colour. This clever optical illusion is achieved through three layers and two surface finishes combined with a galvanic blue coating. The hand-brushed ring where the numerals sit is unique to each watch, changing colour in the light. The numerals are applied to the dial by hand, machined from brass and mirror polished before being coated in Rhodium to give them a brilliant shine. The alternate dots receive the same treatment, catching the light perfectly. Watch the dial being made here . HANDS The Brunswick Blue’s distinctive ‘ Fears ’-shaped hands are finished by a watchmaker, giving them a depth and detail not found in mass-produced, stamped watch hands. Each set of hands is subtly skeletonised before being polished to a mirror shine and plated in Rhodium to match the numerals. Fears is one of only a handful of British watch brands that construct watch hands in-house, in the UK. MOVEMENT The Brunswick is powered by a Swiss made, manual winding ETA 7001 movement. This accurate movement was first designed in the 1970s, and its reliability has ensured its continuing popularity today. We service and finish each movement in Britain, with Côtes de Genève striping and Rhodium plating. Once the movement has been re-assembled and thoroughly tested, it receives Fears’ ‘Golden Pipette’, which is handmade and applied to the bridge. STRAP Each Brunswick Blue is paired with a handmade Bristol Leather strap in Fears Blue . This premium strap uses calf leather that has been vegetable tanned in Britain’s oldest vegetable tannery, Bristol’s Thomas Ware & Sons. Its stainless steel pin buckle is subtly engraved with our ‘Pipette’ logo. The Brunswick is designed to fit all of the straps in our range , which you can easily fit yourself without tools. INDIVIDUALLY NUMBERED Each watch we make carries a unique serial number. Engraved between the 20mm lugs at 12 o’clock, this number helps us identify your watch and its history. BRITISH BOX For decades Fears presented watches in a dark blue box with a cream-coloured lining. We are delighted to continue this tradition today. The Brunswick Blue is presented in a bespoke wooden box, crafted in Britain from English Ash, which is stained Fears Blue. Lined in genuine cream suede, the watch sits proudly on a special cushion. With minimal branding, the outside of the lid reveals a hidden map of Brunswick Square when held in a certain light. ENGRAVED PERSONAL TO YOU Fears offers an engraving service whereby a watch can be made personal to its new owner. We work with one of the UK's leading 3D laser engravers who can engrave initials, a date, or a special verse on your watch. Please contact us here to discuss how we can make your watch extra special. watches.name: Brunswick Au
watches.description: The golden Fears watch. Graceful and complex, the curvaceous Brunswick Au is a particularly exacting object to create. It takes its inspiration from a gentleman’s cushion case watch in the Fears archives, first made in 1924 , which is then realised in exquisite 18ct gold. Case : 38mm, 18ct yellow gold (750), polished, 20mm lug width Dial : Crimson red colour, with gilt printing and hand applied numerals Strap : Oxblood red, premium calf leather, handmade Movement : LJP D100, time only, manual winding Water Resistance : 30 metres (3 ATM) Built to order : >6 months from placing order CASE The Brunswick Au’s elegant 38mm cushion-shaped case is made from solid 18ct Gold. Crafted in the traditional way, entirely from this rich yellow-gold metal, its creation is a process requiring great skill, and the graceful curves of each watch case take over 100 hours to shape and polish. The case and the solid caseback each bear hallmarks from the London Assay Office, and, following a Fears tradition, these comprise the initials of the Managing Director when the watch was built, in this case: ‘NBS’ for our (4th) Managing Director, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill. The Brunswick Au is manually wound each day using a traditional ‘onion’-shaped winding crown, also made from solid Gold, and into which is set a D-colour, flawless diamond, which on Fears watches signifies a case made entirely from precious metal. DIAL The Brunswick Au features a Crimson Red toned dial, along with delicate, vertical brushing, applied by hand, making each watch unique. At six o’clock is the sunken sub-seconds, finished in concentric circles. The numerals receive their own are expertly gold-plated, before being applied by hand, and these, together with the finishing of the dial, create, in the right light, the illusion of a shimmering deep burgundy colour.. watches.description: Important Notice; t he Fears Garrick is an extremely limited-production model with a maximum of 2 build slots available per year - orders placed now will be for delivery August 2027 The superlative Fears watch. The Fears Garrick watch involves a considerable amount of hand-making and hand-finishing and as such they are made in very small batches (of less than 5 a year). Made in partnership with Garrick Watch Co. The result of three years of painstaking design, development and testing is a hand-made watch of exceptional quality and refinement, containing details and flourishes found on haute horology timepieces. CASE The Fears Garrick’s curvaceous 42mm case is made and finished in Garrick’s Norfolk workshops and uses lines with delicate flares which ensure it wears extremely elegantly. The curved sides of the meticulously polished 904L stainless steel case help the slender watch slip easily under a shirt cuff. Slim as well as curvaceous, the watch sits close to the wrist with turned down lugs ensuring a comfortable fit on all sizes of wrist. The Fears Garrick is manually wound each day using a bespoke crown that gives a controlled feel to the precise wind. DIAL The Fears Garrick features an Old English White dial, with a fine matt texture that is reminiscent of traditional paper. This clean, smooth, bright surface is the base for the many minute design details that combine to give the Fears Garrick its technical feel. Deep glossy black printing is combined with seven lines of blood red on the power reserve display at 2 o’clock. These lines represent the moment when the watch’s main spring has wound down. Across from this display at 10 o’clock is the running seconds, which is sunken into the dial with a crisp diamond cut bevel around its edge that is coated in precious Rhodium to draw the eye. This same effect is replicated on the opening at 6 o’clock where the movement’s balance is visible as it rotates back and forth. Applied by hand to the dial’s surface are the diamond-cut numerals, produced in our bespoke ‘Edwin’ typeface. Each numeral is treated like a precious gem in its cutting and polishing before receiving a coat of Black Gold, a special, warm alloy that changes in the light. HANDS The Fears Garrick features the distinctive ‘Fears’-shaped hands, which are hand-finished by a watchmaker, giving them a depth and detail not found in mass-produced, stamped watch hands. Each set of hands is subtly skeletonised before being thermally blued by flame. This traditional method of thermally hardening the steel results in a unique shade of blue that turns from almost black to electric blue in the light. MOVEMENT Visible through the Fears Garrick’s exhibition case back is the exclusive, manual winding Garrick UT-G04 movement. Based on the Garrick UT-G01 that was presented in 2017, this iteration of the movement features a power reserve indicator at 2 o’clock. Exclusive to Garrick, the UT-G04 is hand finished to an exceptional level in the Garrick workshop in Norwick. Visible on both sides of the movement are six screwed chatons (with a further three hidden beneath the dial), an indication of its refined execution. The screwed chatons contrast beautifully with the bridges and plates they are fixed upon, which have been hand frosted with polished bevelled edges. The dark shade of the Rhodium plating provides a stylish contrast to the otherwise classic English appearance, and gives a contemporary feel to the movement's details. Visible through the case back are the two screwed cocks along with the Garrick click. This gracious click ensures a precise and satisfying wind when the movement is powered by hand. All finished to an exacting standard by expert hands. The balance wheel, made from Garrick’s exclusive alloy Sircumet, is positioned dial side and features a free sprung balance. This type of balance has its timing regulated with the adjustment of timing screws, effectively altering the moment of inertia. The benefits of this system

watches.name: Archival 1930 Small Seconds
watches.description: SOLD OUT The Archival 1930 Small Seconds has sold out, however, you might find one at one of our Fears Authorised Stockists , please contact us here . The rectangular Fears watch. Hand built in Britain. Created to coincide with the 175th Anniversary of the founding of Fears, the Archival 1930 Small Seconds is a proportional recreation of an art deco watch Fears made in 1930 . True to the original, each watch features an original vintage movement. With its elegant form it is a perfect luxury rectangular watch for men or women. CASE The slim, rectangular case has the same elegant proportions as the original made in 1930. The new watch has been increased in size a little while maintaining all the important ratios of the original to suit modern tastes. The case is expertly machined from 316L Stainless Steel, in Germany, to a level usually reserved for precious metals. This precisely milled case is then finished in a combination of linearly brushed and highly polished surfaces. This long, slim watch sits comfortably on the wrist thanks to its curved profile. Just like the 1930 original, both the crystal and case back have a matching curvature that follows the contours of your wrist perfectly. The tip of the winding crown, used to wind the watch each day, is deeply engraved with the Fears ‘pipette’ logo. DIAL A close reproduction of the 1930 original, the dial has a distinctive Art Deco design, reflecting the glittering age in which it was first created. To capture the original’s look and details first the dial’s base is polished and plated in 18ct Yellow Gold, and then the rest of the dial is layered on top. This results in the real gold border shining through the smooth, matte Champagne finish that is treated to a light 18t yellow gold plating. The ‘Deco’ numerals that share the slim proportions of the case are printed in crisp glossy black, giving excellent contrast. We call this concoction of gold, ‘Vintage Champagne’. HANDS Expertly milled before being diamond polished, the solid ‘Fears-shaped’ hands feature a central bevel down their length. This bevel helps them catch the light beautifully. The rich bluing offers great contrast with the light dial that increases legibility and aids telling the time. MOVEMENT The Archival 1930 Small Seconds is powered by an original ‘new old stock’ movement that Fears used in the past. The ETA 717 movements date back to 1935 and having never been used previously have undergone a full reconditioning in the workshop while receiving an upgraded mainspring to improve reliability. Each of these original rectangular movements are thus effectively hand built in the traditional way with each movement taking days to assemble and regulate. Please note With these movements being first machined nearly 90 years ago they do not include modern shock absorbing components. This means the watch can be worn and enjoyed everyday but care must be taken to avoid drops or large bangs as this could upset the timekeeping. We expect timekeeping to be within +/-30 seconds a day, in-keeping with the original specification of the movement. STRAP Each Archival 1930 Small Seconds is paired with a handmade Bristol Leather strap in a traditional Oxblood Red, crafted in an art deco style like the original would have been, with no padding and with ‘box-style’ stitching. This premium strap uses calf leather that has been vegetable tanned in Britain’s oldest vegetable tannery, Bristol’s Thomas Ware & Sons to our own shade of this vintage red tone. The strap is lined in Fears Blue Alcantara®, offering a soft and comfortable feel against the skin. The Strap is fastened with a vintage shaped stainless steel pin buckle, which has received a linear brushing to its sides, matching the finish on the sides of the watch’s case. The final flourish comes in the form of a 1930s Fears logo deeply engrave on the polished top of the buckle. Strap Size Standard: Fits wrists approx. 172 - 206mm (6.7" - 8.1") Shorter: Fits wrists approx. 163 - 195

watches.name: 'Elegantly Understated'
watches.description: The complete published history of Fears Please note: Elegantly Understated is now sold out "Elegantly Understated: 175 years of the Fears Watch Company" by Jane Duffus ~ Complimentary Gift Wrapping ~ All copies of "Elegantly Understated" come wrapped in our Heritage Logo collage tissue paper secured with two 175th anniversary seals. This beautifully bound hardback book, published to coincide with Fears’ 175th Anniversary, charts the history of the company from its founding in Bristol in 1846 by Edwin Fear, through to its closure in the late 70’s, and its subsequent re-founding in 2016 by one of Edwin’s 6th generation descendants, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill. It is a detailed history not only of Britain's oldest watch company, but also of a family business that persevered through numerous world catastrophes such as two world wars and the great depression. The book has a chapter devoted to each of the four managing directors who have been at the helm of the company over the years and contains numerous full colour photographs and illustrations from the Fears archive, of both watches and artefacts, along with maps of the former locations and the logos used by the company in each era. AUTHOR The Bristol-based author, Jane Duffus, is three-times great-niece of Edwin Fear. She has written a book that is consistently engaging and illuminating, and which is the result of over two years of research, which has unearthed many new facts about the company, previously thought lost. Her numerous interviews included members of the Fear family as well as one of the final watchmakers to work for the company in its first incarnation. Jane is author of numerous books, including two volumes of the popular “The Women Who Built Bristol” series. FOREWORD The foreword has been written by Roger Smith OBE, who is widely regarded to be one of the finest watchmaker in the world, hand-crafting watches of exquisite beauty and complexity. He is also the co-founding Chairman of the Alliance of British Watch and Clockmakers, of which Fears is one of the founding members. PUBLISHER The book is expertly printed and bound here in the UK, and is published by Bristol Books, a not-for-profit Community Interest Company which specialises in publishing books on subjects relating to the city of Bristol, in order to both celebrate the city and its heritage and to enrich its culture. DIMENSIONS “Elegantly Understated” traces Fears’ history over the course of 176 beautifully bound pages, is printed on rich 140gsm FSC certified paper, and includes numerous full colour photographs. Height: 27.3cm Width: 22cm Thickness: 2.1cm ISBN-10 1909446289 Please note : There is no VAT charged on books in the UK. If "Elegantly Understated" is purchased outside of the UK additional custom duties & taxes may need to be paid at point of delivery.

Crafted in the traditional way, entirely from this noble silver-white metal, its creation is a process requiring great skill, and the graceful curves of each watch case take over 100 hours to shape and polish. The case and the solid caseback each bear hallmarks from the London Assay Office, and, following a Fears tradition, these comprise the initials of the Managing Director when the watch was built, in this case: ‘NBS’ for our (4th) Managing Director, Nicholas Bowman-Scargill. Made in Germany, and involving over 58 separate production processes, the natural colour of a coating of real Anthracite combines with three surface finishes to result in a dial that changes in the light, giving a two-tone effect. Each dial is hand finished and features a contemporary layout with alternating platinum plated numerals and D-colour, flawless diamonds. This results in a highly polished surface that catches the light which is then finished with a platinum-plated coating that perfectly matches the polished 3D numerals. MOVEMENT The Brunswick Pt is powered by a Swiss-made, manual winding La Joux-Perret D100 movement. This movement is the top-grade version, with an extended 50 hour power reserve and finished with Côtes de Genève and blued screws. Each Brunswick Pt undergoes 250 hours of timings checks and tests before being signed off by our (4th) Managing Director. The watch is also designed to fit all of the straps in our range, which you can easily fit yourself without tools. Shorter Strap? watches.name: Azzuro Blue
watches.description: The summer Fears watch strap Our straps are meticulously handcrafted by a family-run atelier in Belgium specialising in beautiful, premium watch straps. Leather Handcrafted from rare, high-quality Barenia calf leather. This superior leather takes its name from the village of Barr in Alsace, from where it originates. Traditionally used for saddles, this smooth calfskin leather requires a complex tanning process, known by only a small number of craftsmen. First double-tanned in chrome and vegetable dyes, the hides are then soaked in a mix of nine different oils over a six-week process, resulting in its unique texture. Barenia leather is famed for being used by a well-known French luxury leather goods manufacturer in their world-famous handbags. Colour Presented in Azzuro Blue, an Italian named vibrant colour that is halfway between blue and cyan, perfect for the summer. The blue has a contrasting platinum stitch that enhances the summery feel of the strap. Surface Finish Barenia leather’s surface has a smooth exterior, with just a hint of gloss. Its oil-absorbing tanning process causes it to patina over time, which is a quality that the leather is famous for. Lining Lined in our signature Fears Blue Alcantara and embossed with both our logo and ‘Handmade in Belgium’. Buckle Please note; the image shows our legacy buckle whereas this strap is now finished with Fears' new bespoke pin buckle (featuring the Fears Cypher). Size Designed to fit all Fears Redcliff, Brunswick and Archival watches, this strap will also fit any watch with a 20mm lug width . The strap is available in two sizes: Standard fits wrists measuring 178 - 210mm (approx.) Shorter fits wrists measuring 164 - 197mm (approx.) Fit yourself Featuring Quick-Release spring bars , our straps can be fitted and removed from the watch using no tools. This means you can change it over in a matter of moments with no hassle.
